text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Foreign investors are interested in Romanian hotels, officials from the Tourism ministry said.
- The leu's retail rates to the dollar firmed to 6,500/6,950 in past days due to heavy dollar suplly.
CAPITAL
- The foreign investors await facts not words from Romania's government, says the newspaper.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The state might mantain a 40 percent stake in Romania's national telecommunication utility Romtelecom after the second stage of its privatisation, said an official.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The 1997 spring farming campaign will be financed with 1.0 trillion lei, funds to be obtained from the state budget, sindycated loans, or economic agents who want to pay in advance for the crop they intend to buy this year.
General
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper publishes the speech delivered by Romania's former king Michael at Britain's Royal United Services Institute for Defence Studies.
- Some 80 percent of Romanians favour EU membership while 76 percent stand for the country's NATO integration, showed the Eurobarometer.
- Portugal supports Romania in its bid to join NATO, said the Romanian foreign ministry quoting Portuguese officials.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Spain will back-up Romania for its early admission to euro-Atlantic structures, said Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea after his visit to Madrid.
- The Public Works' Ministry will build over 25,000 houses and flats in 1997.
- Romania has 267 orphanages with 33,595 institutionalised children, said the education ministry.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Cleaning the capital city of Bucharest would cost some 10 billion lei. ($=7,032 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
